source_snapshot.title: The rational points of a definable set

binder_order: o-minimal structure S over the real field
X subset of R^n definable in S
for every natural T with 1 <= T
conclusion: The rational-point set is finite, and the real coercion of its cardinality is at most c * T^epsilon.
exactness_notes: Height is max(|a|, b) for the reduced rational a/b and coordinatewise maximum on Q^n, as in Definition 1.3; it is not projective height.
The algebraic part is the union of connected positive-dimensional semialgebraic subsets of X, as in Definition 1.5.
For connected semialgebraic subsets of real space, positive dimension is represented by non-subsingleton; this equivalence remains a later proof obligation, not proof credit in this phase.
The first-version individual-set result is selected, not the uniform family results in Theorems 1.9 or 1.10.
No positivity hypothesis on c is added because Theorem 1.8 states only that a constant exists.
The source convention T >= 1 is explicit, and epsilon = 0 is excluded.
Finiteness is explicit before Set.ncard is used, so Lean's zero convention for ncard of an infinite set cannot weaken the target.
